Add a pair of dice for rolling to determine the movement of the game pieces. Make sure the game looks fun and engaging for players of all ages.

import bpy
import bmesh
import mathutils
from mathutils import Vector, Matrix

# ==============================================================================
# HELPER FUNCTIONS
# ==============================================================================

def make_material(name, diffuse_color):
    """Create a new Principled BSDF material with specified diffuse color."""
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name=name)
    mat.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = diffuse_color
    return mat

def add_cylinder(name, radius, depth, location=(0,0,0), rotation=(0,0,0)):
    """Add a cylinder mesh object."""
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=radius, depth=depth, location=location, rotation=rotation)
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = name
    return obj

def add_cube(name, size, location=(0,0,0), rotation=(0,0,0)):
    """Add a cube mesh object."""
    # size is total width/height/depth
    half = size / 2.0
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=half, location=location, rotation=rotation)
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = name
    return obj

def add_disc(name, radius, depth, location=(0,0,0), rotation=(0,0,0)):
    """Add a disc (cylinder with small depth) mesh object."""
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=radius, depth=depth, location=location, rotation=rotation)
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = name
    return obj

def align_axis_to_vector(obj, axis='Z', target_vector=(0,0,1)):
    """Align an object's local axis to a target world vector."""
    # Ensure object is in world space for calculation
    mat_world = obj.matrix_world
    local_axis = obj.matrix_world.to_quaternion() @ mathutils.Vector(axis)
    target = mathutils.Vector(target_vector).normalized()
    
    if local_axis.dot(target) < -0.9999:
        # 180 degree flip
        rot_quat = mathutils.Quaternion((1,0,0), math.pi)
    else:
        rot_quat = local_axis.rotation_difference(target)
    
    obj.rotation_euler = rot_quat.to_euler()

def boolean_subtract(cutter_name, target_name):
    """Perform boolean subtraction using modifier stack."""
    target = bpy.data.objects[target_name]
    cutter = bpy.data.objects[cutter_name]
    
    # Ensure target is active for modifier addition
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = target
    
    # Add Boolean Modifier
    mod = target.modifiers.new(name="BooleanSub", type='BOOLEAN')
    mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
    mod.object = cutter
    
    # Apply modifier
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
    
    # Remove cutter
    bpy.data.objects.remove(cutter, do_unlink=True)

def boolean_union(target_name, other_name):
    """Perform boolean union."""
    target = bpy.data.objects[target_name]
    other = bpy.data.objects[other_name]
    
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = target
    
    mod = target.modifiers.new(name="BooleanUnion", type='BOOLEAN')
    mod.operation = 'UNION'
    mod.object = other
    
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
    bpy.data.objects.remove(other, do_unlink=True)

def add_bevel(obj_name, width=0.001, segments=2):
    """Add a bevel modifier to an object."""
    obj = bpy.data.objects[obj_name]
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    mod = obj.modifiers.new(name="Bevel", type='BEVEL')
    mod.width = width
    mod.segments = segments
    mod.limit_method = 'ANGLE'
    # Apply to keep geometry simple for this script
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)

class Locator:
    """Helper class to find centers of objects."""
    def __init__(self, obj):
        self.obj = obj
    
    def center_world(self):
        return self.obj.matrix_world.to_translation()
    
    def face_center_world(self, face_type='TOP'):
        """Approximate center of a specific face based on bounding box."""
        # Simple approximation: center + offset along normal
        center = self.center_world()
        # For standard primitives aligned to axes:
        if face_type == 'TOP':
            return center + Vector((0,0, self.obj.dimensions.z/2))
        elif face_type == 'BOTTOM':
            return center + Vector((0,0, -self.obj.dimensions.z/2))
        return center

def average(points):
    """Calculate average of a list of vectors."""
    if not points:
        return Vector((0,0,0))
    avg = Vector((0,0,0))
    for p in points:
        avg += p
    return avg / len(points)

# Rotate board_base so its +Z axis aligns +Z (world).

align_axis_to_vector(obj_board_base, 'Z', (0,0,1))

# Anchor board_base to world origin.
# Cube center is at origin by default in add_cube.
obj_board_base.location = Vector((0,0,0))

# Then move by offset(0,0,0).
obj_board_base.location += Vector((0,0,0))

# Apply material board_green to board_base.
if obj_board_base.data.materials:
    obj_board_base.data.materials[0] = mat_board_green
else:
    obj_board_base.data.materials.append(mat_board_green)

# --- SECTION 2 – Create board grid overlay ---
# Create primitive cube with size 0.300×0.300×0.001 m and name it board_grid.
obj_board_grid = add_cube("board_grid", size=0.300, location=(0,0,0), rotation=(0,0,0))

# Rotate board_grid so its +Z axis aligns +Z (world).
align_axis_to_vector(obj_board_grid, 'Z', (0,0,1))

# Align board_grid.bottom_face to board_base.top_face.
# board_base top face is at z = 0.010 (half of 0.020)
# board_grid bottom face is at z = -0.0005 (half of 0.001)
# Target Z for grid center = 0.010 - 0.0005 = 0.0095
loc_base_top = Vector((0,0, 0.010))
loc_grid_bottom = Vector((0,0, -0.0005))
offset_z = loc_base_top.z - loc_grid_bottom.z
obj_board_grid.location = Vector((0,0, offset_z))

# Then move by offset(0,0,0.001).
obj_board_grid.location += Vector((0,0,0.001))

# Apply material board_white to board_grid.
if obj_board_grid.data.materials:
    obj_board_grid.data.materials[0] = mat_board_white
else:
    obj_board_grid.data.materials.append(mat_board_white)

# Boolean-subtract board_grid from board_base; discard board_grid.
# Note: The prompt mentions grid_lines_width and spacing, but the instruction 
# explicitly says "Boolean-subtract board_grid from board_base". 
# Since board_grid is a single solid block, this will just cut a thin slice off the top.
# To simulate "grid lines" via boolean subtraction as hinted, we would normally create 
# multiple thin cutters. However, the prompt only defines ONE object "board_grid" 
# and says "Boolean-subtract board_grid". I will follow the explicit object instruction.
# If the intent was to carve lines, the prompt would have defined multiple grid_line objects.
# Given "Constraint: grid_lines_width... applied via boolean subtraction logic", 
# and only one object provided, I will perform the subtraction as defined.
# To make it visually distinct as a "grid overlay" cut, I'll assume the prompt implies 
# the grid object IS the cutter.
boolean_subtract("board_grid", "board_base")

obj_piece_blue.location = Vector((0,0,0)) # Anchor to origin
obj_piece_blue.location += Vector((-0.10, -0.10, 0.040)) # Offset
